method: Read-only source/AST, installed vendor text, primary provider docs and authenticated GET allowlist only. No imports constructing models/checkpoints/GPU; no tests or service mutation.

vendor_source.limit: Installed local vendor text; project supported <5 does not pin the exact eventual managed build release.

startup.validation: Provisioning and preload identity loops stream hashes one file at a time. Constructed models are not the provisioned-file count.
startup.path: entry managed_startup -> provision paths; app.main build_app(preload=zero_gpu) -> ModelService.preload_default validates all and loads current plaque default once.

runtime_cache_bounds.key_fields: checkpoint/digest plus execution context; mask includes role
runtime_cache_bounds.inference: Missing selected models are constructed lazily during serialized job execution. The two independent LRUs can retain up to four models in a worker, plus construction transient; model count is not a measured RAM bound. Detector has request-scoped loader.

host_capacity.conclusion: No supported inference that all17 checkpoint bytes are simultaneously resident. Existing startup already follows default-only/lazy strategy. No genuine 17GB>16GB startup conflict proven by current source, and no source change justified solely by file total. Actual one-model construction/CPU-vs-emulated-CUDA peak and multi-request cache lifetime still require managed acceptance.

zerogpu_mechanism.primary_documented: Startup CUDA is emulated; official provider technical reference says captured CUDA placement initially uses CPU tensors, then startup pack writes offloaded weights to disk and releases their RAM; GPU workers load from disk. GPU VRAM is not additional host RAM.
zerogpu_mechanism.limit: This mechanism is provider documentation, not an observed build/runtime of this service; no assumption that every CPU tensor or Python model object is packed.

recommendation: Retain existing bounded at-most-one startup warmup. On an approved first managed run record actual effective host limit and startup peak, then representative sequential request/cache peaks. Only if a measured multi-cache conflict appears, propose an explicit shared low-memory eviction budget across the existing two loaders; do not preload8/17, force CPU, or disable supported model versions without reviewed change.
